name: Cementerio Civil & Almudena execution wall
story: After Madrid fell in March 1939, the eastern wall of the Cementerio del Este (Almudena) became the main place of execution for the city: according to research by historians, close to 3,000 people were shot there between 1939 and 1944, among them the 'Trece Rosas', thirteen young women executed on 5 August 1939. The adjoining Cementerio Civil, for those buried outside the Catholic Church, holds the graves of Republican leaders such as Francisco Largo Caballero, Dolores Ibárruri 'Pasionaria' and Pablo Iglesias, and plaques to the Trece Rosas.
see: Graves and memorials in the Cementerio Civil; the wall of the Almudena cemetery, with a memorial to the victims.
plan: Free; cemetery hours daily. Enter the Cementerio Civil from Calle Carmen Martín Gaite; Metro La Elipa.

vis.label: Access
vis.text: Main paths accessible; narrow paths between graves difficult

boxes.text: The memorial with the names of the executed commissioned in 2018 was altered by the city council in 2019 after disputes over errors in the lists; the number of those executed (c. 2,900–3,000) is based on cemetery records.
